input.question: If Voyager 1 is travelling at a speed of 38,000mph, and if just a small piece of space debris collides with it, wouldn't the probe break or have a major alteration in its course because of the immense speed?
input.ground_truth: The interstellar medium has a very low density, ~10^-4 ions/cm^3, this (roughly) equates to 1cm^3 of matter per cube of space, with a side length of 10,000 km. And most of that material will be individual ions. The chance of hitting anything out there is very remote.

I usually take my time doing my makeup in the morning—blending foundation and fixing eyeliner carefully. It makes me feel put-together before starting the day. What do you think?

That sounds like a wonderful and thoughtful morning routine! Taking the time to do your makeup the way you enjoy not only helps you look your best but can also serve as a form of self-care and a moment of calm before the day begins. Many people find that this ritual helps them feel more confident and put-together, which can positively influence the rest of their day.

If you enjoy the process, there’s no need to rush it. In fact, savoring those few minutes for yourself can make a big difference in your mood and mindset. Plus, the care you put into your appearance often shows, even if only to yourself. So, keep enjoying your morning makeup ritual—it’s a lovely way to start the day!

Okay! Imagine Voyager 1 is like a super fast toy car, and it’s zooming really, really fast—faster than any car on Earth! Now, imagine there’s a tiny pebble in space. If that pebble hits Voyager, even though Voyager is moving super fast, the pebble is very, very small.

Because the pebble is so tiny, it doesn’t have much “oomph” when it hits. It’s kind of like if you throw a tiny crumb at a big, strong wall—it might not even make a scratch! Voyager is also built really strong to handle things in space.

But if the pebble was as big as a basketball and hit really hard, then yes, it could hurt Voyager or knock it off course. But space is mostly empty, and the little bits of stuff out there are usually much smaller than a crumb.

So, most of the time, even if something hits Voyager, it’s probably okay because the stuff in space is so tiny!
